quests.title: Today's prices
quests.concept: Dictionaries: names that look up values
quests.summary: The Pantry's board has said APPLES 4P since Tuesday. Teo Vasko's prices are on his slate: apples 4, lemons 3, and plums, which came down from 6 to 5 this morning. Work payment: 18 p.
lesson: Read the note under the price board, then jack the slate in below it.
A dictionary pairs names with values, inside curly brackets: {"APPLES": 4}. prices["APPLES"] looks up the 4.
prices["PLUMS"] = 5 changes one value and leaves the others alone. That's the line Teo will change tomorrow.
for name in prices: visits each name in the dictionary, in the order they were written.
Each page should read like APPLES 4P: the name, a space, the price and a P.

guide.title: Looking things up by name
guide.text: A dictionary keeps each value under its name. Change one entry; read any of them back.

starter: # TODO: the Kerrigans' cart came up full. Plums are 5 today.
# TODO: a page for every fruit, not only apples
hints: Change the plum price with prices["PLUMS"] = 5 before printing anything.
for name in prices:  then, indented, print(name + " " + str(prices[name]) + "P").
quests.done: Apples, lemons and plums, each at today's price. Tomorrow Teo only has to change one line.
